explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/826: 'Are there infinitely many n such that, for all k ≥ 1, τ(n+k) ≪ k?' The Lean statement asserts ∃ C > 0 such that {n | ∀ k ≥ 1, σ 0 (n+k) ≤ C·k} is infinite, with σ 0 = number of divisors τ. Taking a single implied constant uniform over the infinite family of n is the standard (and only meaningful) reading: if C could depend on n the statement would be trivial, since τ(n+k) ≤ n+k ≤ (n+1)k. Faithful (positive form of a yes/no question).
